title: Eurostat euro-area HICP flash estimate, November 2026 — the last euro inflation print before the 12-17 ECB decision
source: EST: TWO PRIMARIES AGREE ON 2026-12-01, fetched direct 2026-11-16. (1) Eurostat's own October flash page, ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-04112026-ap, carries the header line 'Next release: 1 December 2026' (the same field named the 4 November flash correctly a cycle earlier, FT-eurostat-hicp-flash-2026-11-04-1 PASS). (2) The ECB statistical release calendar, ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/statscal/ges/html/sthicp.en.html, re-fetched 2026-11-16: '01/12/2026 15:00 — Euro area seasonally adjusted HICP flash estimate — Reference period: Nov-2026', with the complete October release at '18/11/2026 12:00' and the complete November release at '17/12/2026 12:00'. Stays estimate: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a non-US statistical agency (every sibling Eurostat entry is filed estimate despite direct primaries for the same reason), and the publication hour is not sourced by Eurostat. Checked 2026-11-16
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-11-16 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, over the single proposal proposals/eurostat-hicp-flash-2026-12-01.from-eurostat-hicp-final-2026-11-18.json, read first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md and now inert (shadowed, left in place). It is the first euro inflation datum after the 10-29 ECB hold and the last before the 12-17 decision; three ECB policymakers told Reuters after 10-29 that a December hike was all but certain barring a sudden collapse in energy prices, and Brent spot has since fallen from about $120 (10-30) to about $91-92 (11-10 to 11-11), so this print is the first test of whether that collapse reaches measured inflation. THE SHAPE TO WATCH: October printed 4.0% flash on energy 20.8%, services 3.3%, core 2.5% (Eurostat 2-04112026-ap). The November base is hard in energy (Nov-2025 energy m/m +0.9%, Eurostat prc_hicp_mmor) and soft in the headline (Nov-2025 m/m -0.3%) and in services (-0.8%, a seasonal fall that recurs), so this ledger pre-computes energy about 17% (band 15-19.7) and headline about 3.7-3.8% (band 3.5-3.9), the first non-accelerating headline since June, with services and core roughly flat at 3.3% / 2.5%. CLOCK: 15:00 CET is the ECB series' stamp, not a Eurostat-sourced hour; with both zones on standard time it is 09:00 ET, and any plausible Eurostat hour lands before the 09:30 ET open; ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS print at 10:00 ET the same day. Impact LOW and symbols empty, deliberately and unchanged: no tracked name carries euro-inflation exposure and no house playbook is rates- or euro-keyed. Filed estimate; it widens caution and licenses nothing.
